vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: flyelep-image-clarity-enhance
Version: 1.0.1

The skill defines a standard HTTP API integration for image enhancement via the Flyelep platform (flyelep.cn). It includes clear instructions for the AI agent to handle authentication via a user-provided `secretKey` in the request headers and explicitly warns against hardcoding sensitive credentials. No indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration to unauthorized endpoints, or prompt injection attacks were found in SKILL.md or _meta.json.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions match its stated purpose (calling Flyelep's image clarity API), but the metadata omits the runtime credential the SKILL.md requires and there are privacy considerations when sending images to an external service.

dimensions.detail: The name and description claim an image clarity enhancement via Flyelep AI; the SKILL.md only instructs making HTTP POST calls to Flyelep's imageClarityEnhance endpoint. This is coherent. Minor inconsistency: the skill metadata declares no required credentials or env vars, but the instructions require a 'secretKey' to be supplied at runtime.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrowly scoped to: collect public image URLs, assemble a JSON payload (imgUrls and enhanceStrength), and POST to the documented Flyelep endpoint with a secretKey header. The instructions do not direct the agent to read unrelated files, system configs, or other secrets, nor to transmit unrelated data. They explicitly warn not to persist the secretKey in skill files.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — nothing is written to disk and no external packages are installed. Low install risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md requires a Flyelep 'secretKey' to be placed in the request header at runtime, but the registry metadata lists no required environment variables or primary credential. This mismatch should be resolved (declare how the secretKey is supplied). Also, the skill requires public image URLs: sending image data/links to an external service has privacy implications.

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. It can be invoked autonomously by the agent (default behavior), which is normal for skills; note that autonomous invocation allows the agent to call the external API when triggered.

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it says: it sends user-provided public image URLs to Flyelep's image clarity API and returns the enhanced image URLs. Before installing or using it, consider the following:

- Credential handling: SKILL.md requires a Flyelep 'secretKey' header but the skill metadata does not declare any required env var. Decide how you will provide the secretKey at runtime (secure prompt, secret manager, or ephemeral input). Do not paste the key into skill files or public repos.
- Privacy: images are sent to an external service. Do not send private, sensitive, or copyrighted images unless you trust Flyelep's terms/privacy policy and have permission to upload them.
- Endpoint verification: confirm the API domain (https://www.flyelep.cn) and TLS certificate are legitimate for the service you expect; be wary of typosquatting domains.
- Autonomy: the agent can call the API autonomously when invoked; if you want manual control, restrict when and how the skill is used.
- Operational limits: the API may have timeouts, rate limits, or file-size/format restrictions; follow the documented image specs and handle error codes (401, 405, etc.).

If you want higher assurance, request the publisher to update metadata to declare how the secretKey should be provided (e.g., a required env var name or a secure runtime prompt) and to include a homepage or official docs link to confirm the API origin.
